shows: B-17s bombing Marsala's town and docks, then Palermo's "docks, shipping and shore installations"; a B-17 with its tail turret shot off making a belly landing (the narration)
note: Before the invasion ("Sicily is doomed"): the Allies' bombing, not the Axis raids the batteries recorded. Probably May-June 1943 (Marsala was bombed heavily in May), inferred; the film gives no date. Palermo from 0:32.

shows: The Eighth Army's advance from the south-east toward Catania; Montgomery on the coast road; civilians; prisoners; then Mussolini and Badoglio (the narration and the story's shot list)
note: Released after Mussolini's fall (25 Jul 1943), inferred from the narration. The upload's caption calls it the invasion of Palermo; the film is the British front in the east, and Palermo is not named.

shows: Palermo harbor, torpedo net open, boat enters; wrecked warehouses, harbor, shipyards; Italian prisoners working; ruins, church, docks; damaged crane (the catalogue's shot list, abridged)
note: US Navy film, catalogue title "Palermo harbor damage by US & German air raids", production date 3 Aug 1943 in the catalogue. Two days after the first Axis raid on the city after its capture (1 Aug, recorded by the 62nd CA (AA)'s Batteries C and D). Which damage is which raid's isn't said: the Allies had bombed the port for months before 22 Jul.

shows: Sunk and listing ships along the pier; LCT "293" loaded with boxes; a sunk ammunition ship and the blasted concrete pier; a warship's bow alongside the dock, read as DE "69"; bombed buildings; civilians at a bombed building; wrecked and sunk ships across the harbour (the catalogue's shot list, abridged)
note: US Navy film, production date 3 Aug 1943 in the catalogue. The ammunition ship and the warship are not identified (a lead: which ships were hit at Palermo on 1 Aug).

shows: Damaged lighthouse; men repairing a hole in the hull of a warship alongside the dock (read as a DE); bombed streets, a US tank, civilians carrying belongings back into town; wrecked ships; a large undamaged dry dock; overturned vessels near the beach (the catalogue's shot list, abridged)
note: US Navy film, production date 3 Aug 1943 in the catalogue. Found through its re-upload by WWIIPublicDomain (a finding aid, not the source). The damaged warship is not identified.

shows: Gun flashes (night action); a fire burning in the distance; destroyers, oilers, LCTs and transports at anchor, the city, shoreline and peaks behind (the catalogue's shot list; its quality note: 'very poor ... no significance except for scenes in harbor')
note: US Navy film, production date 26 Oct 1943 in the catalogue. Naples was raided by night from 21 Oct (Blumenson p. 168); which raid the flashes are is not said. The 67th CA (AA) had passed through Naples 17-18 Oct and was at Caiazzo from 21 Oct.

shows: US troops entering Cecina; then US and French troops moving through Siena, a column held at a road block, a tank driver handing candies to a nun and women, anti-Nazi posters, civilians greeting the soldiers (the catalogue's summary, abridged)
note: Army Signal Corps film, dated 3 Jul 1944 in the catalogue, the day French troops entered Siena (Fisher p. 266). The 67th CA (AA)'s Medical Detachment was in Siena on 5 Jul (army/stations.csv).

shows: 'Pre-invasion loading activities, Pozzuoli, Naples area, Italy; 10 Aug 1944': half-tracks, trucks, tanks and other vehicles in the staging area; vehicles backed onto LSTs; a convoy in the harbour with Vesuvius behind; soldiers given doughnuts before boarding the LSTs; medical troops boarding LCIs (the Signal Corps shot card, read on the card)
note: Army Signal Corps film, 952 ft, silent; the shot card is online, the film itself was not found at the catalogue's usual address. The 106th AAA Bn's Battery D was 5½ mi north-west of Pozzuoli from 18 Jul (rg64-481549976/p0824) and its forward detachment aboard LSTs 313 and 318 in Naples harbour from 9 Aug (rg64-565868906/p1143): the same staging for southern France, a day after the battery boarded and in the next harbour. No unit is named on the card.

shows: Destroyers and LCIs in Naples harbour; a DE laying smoke; landing craft at the rendezvous at dawn; LSTs towing barrage balloons leaving Naples harbour (the catalogue's shot list, abridged)
note: US Navy film, 'Task force forms up Naples harbor for invasion southern France', production date 12 Aug 1944 in the catalogue: the day the 106th AAA's Battery D (LSTs 313 and 318) sailed (army/stations.csv). The LSTs filmed are not identified.

shows: The southern France beaches under bombardment on 15 Aug; then LSTs and LCTs loaded in Naples harbour, LSTs loaded with jeeps under barrage balloons, vehicles loaded aboard (the catalogue's shot list, abridged)
note: US Navy film; the catalogue's date (15 Aug 1944) is the landing's: the Naples loading shots are earlier, not dated. The edited sound version is 'Combat Communique No. 5'.

shows: Gen. de Gaulle inspects a line of Goumiers at Venafro: French tricolour on a pole; he shakes hands with some of the men, enters a car and drives off (card: "Silent, 809'"); the same reel has Allied artillery on Cassino, 15 Mar 1944
note: The place and the days: a medical detachment of the 67th CA(AA) is typed at Venafro from 19 Jan 1944 and at Cascano by 15 Mar. The film is of French troops, not the unit, and the card says nothing of who else was there.

shows: Gen. Clark awards decorations to enlisted men after landing on an airfield near Venafro, addresses assembled troops, and presents medals and promotions at Caserta; a band leads the parade after (the card: "Silent")
note: Christmas Day 1943 at the front near Venafro. The 67th CA(AA)'s medical detachment was at Capriati on 19 Dec 1943 and at Venafro by 19 Jan 1944: the same area, a month early. Not the unit.

shows: British and American (30th Infantry, 3rd Division) vehicles move through bomb-damaged Battipaglia; bomb-wrecked railway yards; Gen. Clark and Air Marshal Tedder; Eboli's sign and ruins, people searching them (the card: "Silent")
note: Battipaglia as the Allies found it on 24 Sep 1943, nine months before Battery D, 106th AAA was typed 2 mi W of it on 9 Jul 1944. The town, not the unit.

shows: Warships fire at the Sicilian coast; men go down landing nets; landing craft in the surf; troops, ammunition, vehicles on the beach; a pontoon causeway to an LST at Gela; an LST burning after enemy bombing; wrecked landing craft and wrecked German railway guns around Licata harbour (the card: "July 1943", "Silent")
note: The beaches where the 62nd CA(AA)'s batteries landed by sea at Gela on 19 Jul 1943 and Licata on 23 Jul. The card gives only the month, so these may be the first days of the landing (inferred: Patton's landing; the card does not say), not the batteries' own. Not the unit.

shows: US tanks along the Tiber, crowd round a tank, infantry on tanks crossing the Tiber, scout car passing the Vatican, vehicles passing the Colosseum (card: "Entry into Rome, 5 June 1944"; "Silent"); the Pope addresses St Peter's Square ("June 1944")
note: The day Rome was entered. A medical detachment of the 67th CA(AA) was typed at Artena on 5 Jun 1944 and at Marino on 10 Jun, south-east of Rome. Not the unit, and not Rome.

archive_id: British Movietone story (number not in the upload's description)
shows: Aerial shots of Naples "crammed with equipment for invasion of South of France"; troops marching across beaches; paratroops dropping; sea-landed troops; then the liberation of Marseille with British troops, the FFI and French troops (the story's shot list)
note: Naples as the Dragoon force gathered, in the days before the landings of 15 Aug 1944; Battery D, 106th AAA sailed from Naples on 12 Aug. The date is inferred from the story's own text (the invasion of the south of France); the upload's title and its 28 Aug 1944 date are a modern caption for Marseille's liberation, not the film's. A British newsreel, not the unit; the aerial Naples shots have no stated day.

shows: Troops of the 150th Signal Company, 10th Armored Division, whitewash a half-track and a 2 1/2-ton truck in a street (the card: "PAINTING VEHICLES, Metz, France - 13 Jan 45", "Silent"). The reel goes on to St. Hubert and Bastogne, Belgium.
note: Metz a week before the Nancy and Toul gun defenses moved into the city's defenses (20 Jan 1945, aar3/p097: the 128th AAA Gun Bn), and the day after the 9th Armored Division came to Thionville (12 Jan, aar3/p556; command post at Ennery, about 12 km north of Metz, from 14 Jan). Snow camouflage on another division's vehicles; neither unit is in the film. Card read on the scan.

shows: "CUs, skis on L-4 plane. Excellent scenes, L-4 plane equipped with skis, taxiing on field, in flight and landing" (the card: "CUB SKIS, Thionville, France - 15 Jan 45", "Silent"). The reel opens with an awards ceremony in Italy.
note: Thionville three days after the 9th Armored Division moved there (12 Jan 1945, aar3/p556); its command post was at Bockange from 12 Jan and Ennery from 14 Jan (etoob-9AD/p503-504). Whose L-4 is not said; not the division's own film. The snow on the ground at mid-January. Card read on the scan.

shows: "MSs, CUs, soldiers load white snow capes into trucks. Ints, French Red Cross workers making large Red Cross insignia for US medics. CU, women cut up German flags. Ext, Frenchwoman and US officers collect vests at Red Cross center" (the card: "RED CROSS VESTS, Thionville, France, 31 Jan 45", "Silent"; card 2 of 2). The reel also has Luzon, the Monschau Forest and Liege.
note: Thionville on 31 Jan 1945, the date of Third Army's antiaircraft situation map with the 9th Armored Division and the 128th AAA Gun Bn in the Metz gun-defense circle (aar3/p098); the 9th Armored came to Thionville on 12 Jan (aar3/p556). French civilians and the snow capes of late January; which unit's medics is not said, and the division is not named. Card read on the scan.

shows: Seabees ("CB's") lay and join sewer pipe, mix concrete, build a shack's foundation and floor, saw planks; a bulldozer pulls a material carrier; a freighter unloads supplies to the dock, civilians receive them, CBs load trucks and drive off (the catalogue's shot list, abridged)
note: US Navy film, production date 13 Jan 1943 in the catalogue. The 20th Naval Construction Battalion was at Nouméa from October 1942 to June 1943, unloading the ships (seabees/projects/noumea-port.md); the film does not name the battalion, and other Seabee units were at Nouméa, so it shows the place and the work, not the 20th. Found through its re-upload by WWIIPublicDomain (a finding aid, not the source).

place: New Georgia, en route to Viru Harbor
shows: Infantrymen of Co B, 103d Infantry, load ammunition, barracks bags and equipment into landing craft, go out to the destroyer Kilty, eat C rations on deck, and go over the side by cargo nets into landing craft that head for the shore (the shot card, 462-1; the rest of the reel is King George VI at Oran)
note: Signal Corps film; the shot card dates it 24 June 1943 and titles it "New Georgia Island--en route to Viru Harbor". The Viru landing force a week before the 20th's Viru company landed there (2 July 1943; seabees/projects/viru-railway.md): the same operation, not the battalion. Where the scenes were shot (the harbour of departure) the card doesn't say.

shows: A crane hoists an engine into a PT boat; PT boats on the ways and in floating drydocks, propellers on racks; a practice torpedo launched, its wake, the spent torpedo hoisted to a barge (the catalogue's shot list, abridged)
note: US Navy film, title "PT boats & operations; practice torpedo exercises, PT base, Rendova"; the catalogue gives no date. January 1944 is inferred from the next film, 428-NPC-1817 (PT boat operations at Rendova Point, catalogue date 1944-01), and the re-uploader's title gives 22-28 Jan 1944 (WWIIPublicDomain, a finding aid, unconfirmed). Which island isn't said: MTB Base Eleven, the PT command's repair base, was on Bau from about January 1944 (seabees/projects/bau-pt-base.md), after the 20th's Bau unit left on 9 January. The base the Seabees prepared, in use; not the battalion.

shows: Men of the 113th Seabees board a truck; bulldozers build a ramp to a beached LST and tow trucks across the reef; a crane lifts a truck from a hole on the beach; Seabees prepare a Bailey bridge, saw logs, drill for dynamite, demolish a brick house (the catalogue's shot list, abridged)
note: US Navy film, production date 7 May 1945 in the catalogue; not online at the Archives. Another battalion (the 113th) doing the same kind of work over Okinawa's reefs while the 20th worked the waterfront and roads (seabees/projects/okinawa-waterfront.md); the beach isn't named. Not the 20th.
